correctness.rationale: Orthonormal first-biased-Walsh basis gives K(x,y)=1+sum_i (xi-p)(yi-p)/[p(1-p)]. Absolute kernel row averages are exact Linfty norm, and symmetry gives L1. For p<=1/2 the all-one row is maximal by convex order between centered two-point laws with minimum -1; strictness of bias comparison for n>=2 is from conditional Jensen at a suitable binomial success count, handling exceptional (n-1)p integer by continuity. Binomial tails and symmetric random-walk identities yield exact fair formula and p to zero limit. CLT with second-moment UI yields the dense sqrt(n) coefficient, while binomial-to-Poisson with UI yields the n-scale sparse formula and derivative jumps. Independent exact kernel row enumeration for n<=6 and grid bias confirmed formulas and monotonicity.
